prereqs
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
```

## Intro

This document is a place for the pipeline to create the Scraps from the Loft data frame. 

## Reading in the Data

The code below shows how to do this with html filling in for a link to the page with the transcript. For the purposes of this document, we can look at the test page I used, the Adults Episode 4 transcript. 


```{r}
html <- "https://scrapsfromtheloft.com/tv-series/adults-s01e04-house-rules-transcript/"

show <- read_html(html)
  #reads in the website
```

## Finding the right Elements and Transformation

Using selector gadget, I was able to find the correct elements I wanted to target fairly quickly as shown in the code below. 

```{r}
show_script <- show |>
  html_elements(".single-content p") |>
  #find all elements on the web page that are actually dialogue
  html_text2()
  #turn those elements into only text

show_df <- data.frame(show_script) 
  #turn our character vector into a df
```

I also transformed this into a data frame. While this probably wasn't strictly necessary, it made it easier to borrow code from the [Santa Barbara Pipeline](santa_barbara_pipeline.qmd) which saved time and energy. Hopefully, it also makes these twin pipelines easier to follow. 

## Cleaning the Data

The next step was to eliminate the first four lines. Luckily, in every transcript the first four lines are dedicated to the same structure, making it easy to leave only the text we want. 

```{r}
show_df <- show_df |>
  slice(-(1:4))
  #removes the first four rows which are not actually dialogue from the show
```


```{r}
clean <- function(string) {
  string |>
  str_replace_all("\\[.*?\\]", "") |>
  #remove a [ followed by any number of any characters and then a ]
  str_replace_all("♪[^♪]*♪", "") |>
  #removes a ♪ followed by any number of characters followed by ♪
  str_replace_all("\\([^)]*\\)", "")
  #removes a ( followed by any number of characters followed by )
}
```


## The Final Function and Iteration

```{r}
get_clean_script <- function(html) {
  
  show <- read_html(html)
  #reads in the website
  
  series <- str_remove(html, "https://scrapsfromtheloft.com/tv-series/") |>
            #removes the first part of the html link which is identical accross transcripts
    str_replace("-s\\d.+-", "-") |>
    #replaces -s followed by a digit followed by any number of characters and then a - with a single -
    str_remove("/") |>
    #removes remaining /
    str_replace_all("-", "_")
    #replaces all -'s with _'s
  
  show_script <- show |>
  html_elements(".single-content p") |>
  #find all elements on the web page that are actually dialogue
  html_text2()
  #turn those elements into only text
  
  show_df <- data.frame(show_script) 
  #turn our character vector into a df
  
  show_df <- show_df |>
  slice(-(1:4))
  #removes the first four rows which are not actually dialogue from the show
  
  #defines a function for cleaning each string in our df
  clean <- function(string) {
  string |>
  str_replace_all("\\[.*?\\]", "") |>
  #remove a [ followed by any number of any characters and then a ]
  str_replace_all("♪[^♪]*♪", "") |>
  #removes a ♪ followed by any number of characters followed by ♪
  str_replace_all("\\([^)]*\\)", "") |>
  #removes a ( followed by any number of characters followed by )
  str_replace("^[A-Z]+ ?[1-9]?:", "")
}
  
  show_df <- show_df |>
    mutate(show_script = 
             clean(show_script)) |>
    #cleans up all the lines with the function above
    mutate(show_script = 
             trimws(show_script)) |>
    #removes extra white space
    filter(!show_script == '') 
    #removes lines with no text
  
  show_df |>
    mutate(script = "x",
         .before = show_script)
  #add a column fill in for unifying these features

  show_df <- show_df |>
  summarize(show_script = str_flatten(show_script, " "))
  #returns a single cell data frame of all of the dialogue combined with spaces
  
  show_df <- show_df |>
  mutate(id = series,
         #adds a new column that gives the id based on the series
         .before = "show_script") |>
  rename("clean_words" = show_script)
  #renames to clean_words so we can rbind this thing with the santa barbara df eventually making one big df!!!
  
  show_df
}

get_clean_script(html)
```


## Deciding on TV shows and Iteration

To compile a list of TV shows I would want to include, I compiled a list of the available TV shows that would be relevant to the study. Their relevance was determined using criteria in the [Project Plan document](project_plan.md). I also included the genre of each show (derived from the Wikipedia site of the TV show) which allowed me to ensure a nearly even number of drama TV shows and comedy TV shows. Since there were only 27 comedy TV shows, I included all of them. I then randomly selected 33 of the remaining drama TV shows with the following code.

```{r}
#| eval: false

set.seed(20)
#just chose a random seed so that we get the same random result every time we run this
dramas <- tv_show_df |>
  filter(str_detect(genre, "drama") & !str_detect(genre, "comedy")) |>
  #filters only shows that included the genre drama and not the genre comedy
  slice_sample(n = 32)
  #randomly selects 32 of these

dramas
```


Finally a compiled a list of the actual html links for each episode. Unfortunately, since each link referred to a specific episode and there was no clear way to know which episodes were included, this process had to be done manually. Once this list of links was compiled, I was able to iterate using the following mapping code. 

```{r}
#| eval: false

x <- episode_links |>
  map(get_clean_script) 

y <- do.call(rbind, x)

y
```


## Overview of the Data

The resulting data frame is made up of the sixty observations of individual scraped webpages The TV show title is listed under the `id` column. In the `clean_wrds` column, the clean text of each page is included. Importantly, these are divided up roughly evenly my genre. I intend to add the genre information to the ID and to get a summary of how many tokens are in each observation as immediate next steps.
